cultural.vision_reason: The image shows a red twill scarf/shawl with dense polychrome embroidery (circular medallion, botehs, floral and hooked motifs) and fringe, consistent with Central Asian embroidered textiles of the Uzbek/Central Asian tradition (suzani-type work).

physical.title: scarf; shawl
physical.summary: A woman's scarf / shawl; square.  Ground made of red/pink twill woven cotton cloth, with two panels of the same fabric, each 9 cms deep, stitched to the bottom two sides.  Polychrome embroidery in lower half of scarf: a large circular motif framed by four large botehs (two different colourways). Circular motif is divided into eight segments - each containing a floral motif - with the same colours opposite: black/orange; orange/blue; pink/green.  Edge of circle has green 'hooked' motifs; further floral and 'hooked' motifs fill out the centre ground.  Line of blue curvilinear designs across widest part of scarf.  White cotton rick rack divides the main ground from the panels, which contain cross stitch embroidery: geometric patterning worked in four different colourways.  A green passementerie trimming stitched to edge (finger braiding?) with plied fringing joined at the bottom and threaded with small white plastic (?) beads.  Panels lined with three different printed cotton cloths (cream/pink): 6 pieces in total.
